spec.full_target: For every nonnegative integer n and every nonempty compact E⊆ℝ^n, with I=[0,1] and E×I equipped with the concatenated Euclidean metric, dim_H(E×I)=dim_H(E)+1.

calculations: Squared concatenated product distance is the sum of squared coordinate distances; coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz. diam(U×J)≤√(diam(U)^2+diam(J)^2).

primitives.meaning: The n-dimensional Euclidean space, with ℝ^0 a singleton.

propositions.statement: For every extended metric space X equipped with a measurable space and its Borel measurable-space structure, every set A⊆X, and every d:NNReal, if ↑d<dimH(A), then Measure.hausdorffMeasure (↑d) A=⊤.

locals.declaration: Choose positive cover diameters r_j≤δ with arbitrarily small q-cost; replace zero-diameter sets by small balls if n>0.
Fix an arbitrary countable δ-cover of F.

locals.type: open interval containing bounded set B_i
locals.declaration: Choose J_i containing B_i with length at most ρ_i+η_i, by enclosing B_i between its infimum and supremum and adding η_i total width.
Let C_s(A,δ) be the infimum of Nat-indexed δ-cover sums of ENNReal diameters to exponent s.

argument.text: Let D=dim_H(E) and let F=E×[0,1] with the stipulated concatenated Euclidean metric. First, 0≤D≤n<∞: for n=0 the ambient space is a singleton. For n>0, compactness gives a bounded box containing E; cover that box by a grid of cubes of side h. For 0<h≤1 the number is at most C h^(−n), for a constant C depending only on the box and n, each cube has Euclidean diameter at most √n h, and for every real m>n their total m-power diameter cost is at most C(√n)^m h^(m−n), tending to zero. The definition of Hausdorff dimension as the critical exponent therefore gives D≤n. In particular D is a finite real number and all subsequent choices of exponents are legitimate. For the upper bound, fix any real q>D. Since D≥0, q>0. The threshold definition of Hausdorff dimension gives H^q(E)=0. Here, explicitly, the scale-δ content is the infimum over Nat-indexed sequences (U_j) with E⊆⋃j U_j and diam(U_j)≤δ of the extended nonnegative sum Σ'j diam(U_j)^q; the Hausdorff measure is the increasing-small-scale limit of these contents (the pinned convention has no normalization factor). Thus for each δ>0 and each ζ>0 there is such a cover with total q-cost below ζ. Empty sets may be removed. At n=0, F is isometric to [0,1], so its dimension is 1 and the theorem follows directly; this branch is taken before any positive-diameter replacement. Hence suppose n>0. For any zero-diameter nonempty member U_j choose a point u_j∈U_j and replace U_j by an open Euclidean ball centered at u_j with positive diameter r_j≤δ; choose the radii so their q-costs sum to less than any prescribed additional ζ (for countably many indices, assign the j-th replacement cost <ζ2^(−j)). Keep positive-diameter members, and write r_j for their diameters; the resulting cover has 0<r_j≤δ and arbitrarily small Σj r_j^q. Take δ≤1. Partition [0,1] into at most 1/r_j+1 closed intervals of lengths at most r_j. Their products with U_j cover U_j×[0,1]. In the concatenated metric, squared distance is the sum of squared coordinate distances, so diam(U_j×K)≤√(r_j²+r_j²)=√2 r_j. Consequently the total (q+1)-power cost of all these product sets is bounded by Σj(1/r_j+1)(√2 r_j)^(q+1)≤2(√2)^(q+1)Σj r_j^q, since r_j≤1. Their diameters are ≤√2δ. As the original q-cost and replacement cost can be made arbitrarily small, the (q+1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure of F is zero. The dimension threshold implication gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. This holds for every q>D, and taking the infimum over q>D yields dim_H(F)≤D+1.

For the lower bound when D>0, fix a real s with 0<s<D. Let C_a(A,δ) denote exactly the infimum of Σ'i (ediam U_i)^a over Nat-indexed covers (U_i) of A with ediam(U_i)≤δ for all i. Here ediam takes values in ENNReal, and a>0 is interpreted through its NNReal/ENNReal coercions; 0^a=0. From the pinned formula for Hausdorff measure, H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0} C_a(A,δ)=lim_{δ↓0}C_a(A,δ): both use the same Nat-indexed cover sequences, the same ediam diameter cutoff, and the same tsum, and the formula's supremum over nonempty-member witnesses contributes the term ediam(U_i)^a for nonempty U_i and zero for empty U_i, equal to that term since ediam(∅)=0. For δ1≤δ2, the admissible δ1 covers are a subset of the δ2 covers, so C_a(A,δ1)≥C_a(A,δ2); hence the decreasing-scale limit equals the supremum over positive δ. The dimension threshold theorem applied at NNReal exponent s says H^s(E)=∞ because (s:ENNReal)<dim_H(E). Therefore C_s(E,δ) tends to ∞ as δ decreases to zero. Fix 0<δ≤1 and an arbitrary Nat-indexed δ-cover (V_i) of F; discard empty members and put ρ_i=ediam(V_i)≤δ. Let A_i and B_i be its coordinate projections. The coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the concatenated metric, so ediam(A_i),ediam(B_i)≤ρ_i. Choose η_i=ε·2^(−(i+1))/(1+ρ_i^s)>0, so Σ'i η_iρ_i^s≤ε, and choose an open interval J_i containing B_i with length at most ρ_i+η_i. Such an interval exists because B_i is bounded (its diameter is at most finite ρ_i); take an interval extending each side of its infimum/supremum by a total additional width no more than η_i. For every t∈[0,1], the A_i with t∈J_i cover E: if x∈E then (x,t) lies in some V_i; thus x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Each A_i has diameter ≤δ, so the definition of C_s gives pointwise C_s(E,δ)≤Σ'i 1_{J_i∩[0,1]}(t)ρ_i^s. Each summand is a nonnegative ENNReal-valued measurable function on [0,1] with restricted Lebesgue measure, since J_i∩[0,1] is Borel. Integrate this pointwise inequality: monotonicity of the ENNReal lintegral gives C_s(E,δ)≤∫⁻_{[0,1]} Σ'i 1_{J_i∩[0,1]}ρ_i^s. Countable Tonelli, applied to these AEMeasurable summands, identifies the integral with Σ'i ∫⁻ 1_{J_i∩[0,1]}ρ_i^s. The integral of each indicator is the measure of J_i∩[0,1], namely its interval length clipped to [0,1], and is at most ρ_i+η_i; the restricted Lebesgue measure of [0,1] is one. Thus C_s(E,δ)≤Σ'i(ρ_i+η_i)ρ_i^s≤Σ'iρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Terms with ρ_i=0 vanish because s>0. Since ε>0 was arbitrary, C_s(E,δ)≤Σ'iρ_i^(s+1) for every chosen cover V_i. Taking the infimum over all such covers gives C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). As δ↓0 the left side tends to infinity, so the right side does also; the exact scale-content formula then gives H^(s+1)(F)=∞. The dimension threshold implication in the reverse direction yields s+1≤dim_H(F). This holds for every 0<s<D; taking the supremum over those s proves D+1≤dim_H(F). All scalar use of the threshold results is at NNReal exponents: s is represented by its NNReal coercion and the measure formula uses the corresponding real coercion, with no identification of distinct scalar types suppressed.

If D=0, choose x₀∈E by H001. Define p:F→[0,1] by p(x,t)=t. Since |t−u|≤((|x−y|²+|t−u|²))^(1/2), p is 1-Lipschitz. It is onto because p(x₀,t)=t for every t∈[0,1]. Apply the general Lipschitz image dimension inequality to p and the set F: dim_H([0,1])=dim_H(p(F))≤dim_H(F). The interval dimension is 1: [0,1] has nonempty interior in the one-dimensional real vector space, so the pinned theorem Real.dimH_of_nonempty_interior gives dimension finrank_R(R)=1. Therefore dim_H(F)≥1=D+1. This branch includes n=0, but the direct n=0 isometry branch in S001 already handled the upper bound without any positive-diameter replacement. Combining this lower bound when D=0, the slicing lower bound when D>0, and the upper bound for all D proves dim_H(F)=dim_H(E)+1.

The map (x,t)↦t has Lipschitz constant 1 since |t-u|≤sqrt(|x-y|²+|t-u|²).
ℝ has its usual real normed additive commutative group and real normed-space structures.
ℝ is finite-dimensional over ℝ with finrank 1.
